findings.title: Wrong substring indices and inverted boolean condition in `isAccessTokenId` matcher
findings.body:
In `AssertEvents.isAccessTokenId`, the check `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` has two bugs:
1. The encoded context prefix is 6 characters long (`<2-char sessionType><2-char tokenType><2-char grantType>`), so the grant type shortcut is at indices `(4, 6)` (matching `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId` line 81), not `(3, 5)`.
2. The equality check is not negated (`equals` instead of `!equals`), so it returns `false` when the substring matches the expected shortcut and `true` when it does not. The test only passes right now because `substring(3, 5)` extracts the wrong characters (e.g., `"ta"` from `"onrtac"`), which never equals `expectedGrantShortcut`.

findings.title: `AccessTokenContext` constructor checks `grantType` for null twice instead of checking `rawTokenId`
findings.body: Line 73 calls `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");` instead of `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`. As a result, a `null` `rawTokenId` is silently accepted and stored in `AccessTokenContext`, rather than throwing a `NullPointerException` with the intended message.

findings.title: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` accepts `"un"` (`UNKNOWN`) shortcuts for session type and token type
findings.body: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.init` populates `sessionTypesByShortcut` and `tokenTypesByShortcut` using `SessionType.values()` and `TokenType.values()`, which include `SessionType.UNKNOWN("un")` and `TokenType.UNKNOWN("un")`. Consequently, `getTokenContextFromTokenId("ununac:1234")` resolves `st` and `tt` to `UNKNOWN` instead of rejecting the token ID as invalid, even though `encodeTokenId` explicitly forbids encoding `UNKNOWN` for `SessionType` or `TokenType`.

findings.title: Potential `NullPointerException` in `OAuth2GrantType.Context` constructor when `formParams` is null
findings.body: In `OAuth2GrantType.Context`, `this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);` dereferences `formParams` unconditionally. If `Context` is constructed before form parameters are parsed or in a test/caller passing `null` (note that `setFormParams` exists on `Context`), this will throw a `NullPointerException`. Also, `setFormParams` does not update `this.grantType` when form parameters are replaced.

findings.title: Javadoc for `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` says 3-letters shortcut, but implementation requires 2 characters
findings.body: The Javadoc on `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` states `@return usually like 3-letters shortcut of specific grants`, whereas `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` strictly requires the total encoded context to be 6 characters with each grant shortcut being exactly 2 characters (lines 74-81). A custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` implementer following the Javadoc and returning a 3-letter shortcut will cause `getTokenContextFromTokenId` to fail with `IllegalArgumentException: Expected length of 6`.
